dependsOnUnavailable: this instance declares no `canonicalUrl`, and §3.4's record is `{packageId, version, uri}` — `canonicalUrl` is what plays `uri`, so the record cannot be expressed rather than being withheld on purpose

@graph.name: math-md-authoring
@graph.title: Math markdown authoring
@graph.description: The math half of the harness's md-authoring: display and inline math, KaTeX limits, math in titles and table cells, and what the LaTeX pipeline does with tables, for a paper folio's .md blocks.

@graph.name: lean-toolchain-contract
@graph.title: Lean toolchain — the role's contract

@graph.name: paper-chapter-complexity
@graph.title: Paper chapter complexity and block density
@graph.description: The paper-folio half of the harness's chapter-complexity-review and block-density skills: the mathematical block-kind classifier for logical vs. storytelling backward edges, cross-paper uses[] filtering, and table-extraction and density rules for formal statement blocks.

@graph.name: formal-layer-editing
@graph.title: Formal-layer editing
@graph.description: The formal-layer half of the harness's editor: the heavy-proof discipline, the routing rows for formal requests, the proof-block workflow and the pre-merge formal audits, for a paper folio with a Lean layer.

@graph.name: paper-voice-audit
@graph.title: Paper voice audit and watcher rules
@graph.description: The paper-folio half of the harness's one-voice-audit, one-voice-integration-watcher, and one-voice-style-guide: scholarly voice across proof bodies, pdflatex Unicode crash remediation, mathematical hedging patterns, conditional-theorem banners, and paper watcher triggers.

@graph.name: math-readability-editing
@graph.title: Math readability editing
@graph.description: The math half of the harness's readability-editing: math-specific style checks, the blueprint and formal-proof index cross-checks, and the mandatory TeX snippet validation after editing a paper folio's blocks.

@graph.name: formal-accuracy
@graph.title: Formal accuracy
@graph.description: The accuracy checks a content type with a formal-proof layer adds to the harness's scientific-accuracy review: the consequence-versus-axiom audit, formal cross-references, and validation across the .ts / .md / formal triple.

@graph.name: milnor-exposition-standard
@graph.title: The Milnor exposition standard
@graph.description: The eight hallmarks of mathematical exposition, scored 0-2 with sixteen the only passing total, derived from John Milnor's "Link Groups" (1954). The author-facing half of the `expo-milnor-clarity` strict gate; three of its findings contradict the general house voice and say so.

@graph.name: build-pdf
@graph.title: /build-pdf
@graph.description: Builds a paper folio's PDF locally in the workspace — the monolithic PDF plus split per-chapter PDFs.

@graph.name: verify-local-substrate
@graph.title: Verify Anchor Connectivity
@graph.description: Verify that every result block of a designated class traces back to a designated anchor definition through the uses[] dependency graph. Identifies gaps where claims lack a formal connection to the anchor, and suggests fixes.

@graph.name: remark-audit
@graph.title: Remark Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit remarks for provable content. Every remark must interpret a mathematical statement that can be formalized in Lean. Detects dangling remarks (no `interprets` link), ambiguous domain terms, and missing formalization.

@graph.name: lean-content-test
@graph.title: Lean content test
@graph.description: The paper-folio half of the harness's content-test: run Lean proof verification and LaTeX compilation, dispatch the repo's Lean CI, and check how much of the corpus a Lake build reaches before reading its numbers.

@graph.name: rendering-auditor
@graph.title: Rendering Auditor
@graph.description: Multi-pass rendering auditor for content blocks. Validates markdown+TeX syntax, notation consistency, compilation, layout, and visual output across both HTML and PDF pipelines. Used by author agents after edits and as part of QC reports.

@graph.name: proof-gap-audit
@graph.title: Proof Gap Audit
@graph.description: Audit individual proofs and the network of proofs for gaps. Detects intra-proof gaps (unproved assertions, existence without proof, uniqueness asserted but not shown, hand-waving, missing citations) and inter-proof gaps (missing bridging lemmas, broken chains of implication, unstated propositions needed to tie results together).

@graph.name: lean-cache-restore
@graph.title: Lean cache: the authoring loop
@graph.description: The Lean build loop — restore a warm cache before working, and contribute your build back when done. One command each. A restore is ~2 minutes; a cold Mathlib build is 30-60.

@graph.name: critical-path-analysis
@graph.title: Critical Path Analysis & Context Review
@graph.description: Analyse the critical path of the paper's argument chain, audit statement and proof contexts (e.g. general vs specialised assumptions), identify blocks that need rewriting, and propose cleanups.  Also covers "statement and proof context review" — classifying each result by whether its statement, proof, or both require specialisation assumptions.

@graph.name: formalizer
@graph.title: Lean 4 Formalizer (Narrative to Proof)
@graph.description: Lean 4 Formalizer — translates the logical skeleton of narrative mathematical proofs into Lean 4 tactic blocks.  Uses the Ontologist's glossary to resolve types, maps narrative proof phrases to Lean tactics, and generates sorry-bridged partial proofs that compile.

@graph.name: lean-formal-graph
@graph.title: Lean formal dependency graph
@graph.description: Build and query the FORMAL dependency graph — what a proof actually invokes, derived from `lean.ref`. Distinct from `uses[]`, which is editorial. Use for impact analysis, exposition gaps, and declaration ownership.

@graph.name: lean-build-fix
@graph.title: Lean Build Fix Skill
@graph.description: Iteratively fix Lean build errors and linter warnings until the build passes cleanly. Uses MCP diagnostics when available, falls back to parsing lake build output.

@graph.name: proof-editor
@graph.title: Proof Editor (Coordinator)
@graph.description: Coordinator skill for proof review and repair. Runs the full proof skill suite (gap audit, lean review, completeness, simplifier, triage), deduplicates findings across reviewers, ranks by severity and dependency order, and delivers a single author-ready action plan with concrete suggested edits (never applying them without author approval).

@graph.name: compute-integration-watcher
@graph.title: Compute Integration Watcher
@graph.description: Cross-layer wiring auditor — watches for newly-landed formal/analytic improvements (proofs, propositions, lemmas, axiom→theorem upgrades, witness data) on the default branch AND on open PRs, and checks whether each one has been wired into the production compute chain. Complements `compute-audit` (which scans for performance/correctness antipatterns inside scripts). Runs in two modes: REACTIVE (watch new commits / PR events) and IDLE-SWEEP (walk all existing content blocks and audit wiring).

@graph.name: compute-audit
@graph.title: Compute Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit compute scripts for a catalogue of correctness and performance antipatterns. Distinguishes CORRECTNESS antipatterns from PERFORMANCE antipatterns. Produces a ranked workplan citing concrete files+lines.

@graph.name: proof-triage
@graph.title: Proof Triage & Resolution
@graph.description: Systematically triages and resolves `sorry` stubs across the Lean codebase. Inventories all sorry sites, orders them by dependency, attempts proofs using mathlib/library search, and escalates to a proof writer with similar-lemma suggestions when stuck.

@graph.name: proof-conciseness
@graph.title: Proof Conciseness
@graph.description: Tighten narrative (human-readable) proofs without changing mathematical content. Targets verbose prose patterns in `.md` proof files — padding phrases, re-explained elementary steps, redundant restatement, long case analyses that collapse into tables. Complements proof-simplifier (Lean tactics) and readability-editing (chapter prose); this skill operates on the proof block's `.md` specifically and preserves every logical step.

@graph.name: lean-witness-audit
@graph.title: Lean Witness Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit computation scripts (typically Python) that produce witness statements for Lean formalization. Verify witnesses are complete, self-documenting, use paper notation, link to a content block, and emit Lean-compatible declarations. Detects staleness via script content hash and git commit SHA.

@graph.name: proof-exposition-review
@graph.title: Proof Exposition Review
@graph.description: Paper-wide retrospective review of a single proof block. Given the current state of the paper — including all blocks added since the proof was written — suggest simplifications to the statement, proof, or surrounding exposition. Complements proof-simplifier (which operates on 2-4 block local clusters) by considering the full dependency graph and all recently-added content.

@graph.name: groebner-basis
@graph.title: Gröbner Basis Skill
@graph.description: Compute Gröbner bases and normal forms for (possibly non-commutative) algebraic structures using a CAS (e.g. Singular letterplace) or an instrumented project routine. Reduce words to normal form with step-by-step logging, extract invariants, and emit witness JSON.

@graph.name: lean-mathlibext-curator
@graph.title: `MathlibExt` Curator Skill
@graph.description: Curate `<Paper>/MathlibExt.lean` — the staging area for upstream- candidate lemmas (List/sort plumbing, Foldl/foldr at Monoid level, Real-function bridges).  Decide what lives in `MathlibExt` vs inline, and tag candidates with `-- TODO upstream: …`.

@graph.name: latex-build-cache
@graph.title: LaTeX build performance — findings + what's safe
@graph.description: LaTeX build performance. What works is the iterative loop: a static preflight with no TeX, Tool `tex-install` for an engine, Tool `paper-feature-build` for quick changed-chapter builds with latexdiff, then the full build. Both standard preamble/diagram caching mechanisms failed on this toolchain, so there is no cache; read the negative results before attempting one.

@graph.name: lean-proof-vacuity-audit
@graph.title: lean-proof-vacuity-audit
@graph.description: Detect and fix Lean "vacuous proof" anti-patterns — declarations that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and whose statement matches the .md, yet carry NO mathematical content (they assume what they claim, conclude something trivially true, or rest on a false premise). These slip past `proof-statement-integrity` (which only checks signature-stability + an axiom sweep), so detection is semantic and agent-checked. Use when auditing Lean for circular / vacuous / trivially-true proofs, after a batch proof-statement-integrity normalization (the batch "wrap the conclusion in a structure field and project it" fix produces these), or when a "theorem" looks too easy. Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `proof-no-*` criteria.

@graph.name: proof-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /proof-integration-watcher
@graph.description: Proof-QA integration watcher — watches origin/main + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for narrative-proof (`.md`) or Lean-proof (`.lean`) changes, runs the proof QA skill suite on every detected change, queues gaps, attempts auto-discharge for easy sorries / naked conjectures with provable scaffolding, and escalates the rest to the author. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol) from `integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: semantic-review-scoping
@graph.title: Semantic review scoping
@graph.description: Decide what to review FIRST. Computes which blocks' semantic correctness can actually affect a target theorem, so agent-adjudicated criteria are spent where they matter instead of swept in file order.

@graph.name: proof-status-tracking
@graph.title: Proof Status Tracking
@graph.description: Maintain the proof-objects.json manifest tracking formalization status, review records, and LaTeX-to-Lean linkages.  Generate status dashboards and enforce review policies.

@graph.name: lean-generation
@graph.title: Lean File Generation
@graph.description: Extract theorem-like objects from LaTeX source and generate corresponding Lean 4 stub files with `sorry` placeholders.  Maintains the proof-objects.json manifest linking LaTeX labels to Lean declarations by doc-gen4 URL.

@graph.name: build-docs
@graph.title: /build-docs
@graph.description: Builds the Lean HTML documentation (doc-gen4) locally in the workspace, for any paper folio's Lean package.

@graph.name: detangler-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /detangler-integration-watcher
@graph.description: Structural-QA integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for organisational changes (paper / chapter manifest edits, new blocks, edited `uses[]` / `kind` / `label` / `interprets` / `defines` / `tags`, block renames) and runs the editor's detanglement skill suite (`content-graph`, `chapter-complexity-review`, `block-density`, `critical-path-analysis`) on every detected change. Queues findings, auto-discharges mechanical fixes (table extraction), routes block reorderings through narrative review before applying them, and escalates section splits / merges / cross-chapter moves / new sections to the author. Inherits shared mechanics from `integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: latex-compilation
@graph.title: LaTeX Compilation Skill
@graph.description: Compile LaTeX source documents into PDF using latexmk and pdflatex, with safe shell-escape isolation across trusted and untrusted environments.

@graph.name: ffi-roundtrip-audit
@graph.title: FFI roundtrip audit
@graph.description: Audit compute scripts for script ↔ native ping-pong patterns — loops that cross the FFI / subprocess boundary per iteration, instead of one boundary crossing for the whole pipeline. Each occurrence forfeits a meaningful fraction of wall time to marshalling + script-side combine overhead. Performance-only — no correctness change.

@graph.name: content-block-review
@graph.title: Content Block Review
@graph.description: Reviews existing content blocks for adherence to all requirements — structural integrity, Lean proof rules, cross-reference consistency, status accuracy, and naming conventions. Flags violations with actionable diagnostics.

@graph.name: uses-formal-comparison
@graph.title: `uses[]` against the formal graph
@graph.description: How a paper folio's formal dependency graph (from Lean) relates to the editorial `uses[]` relation the harness's uses-editorial-review audits: why they diverge, why `uses[]` is never populated from Lean, and how to read the advisory `uses-formal-coverage` finding.

@graph.name: devils-advocate-paper
@graph.title: Devil's advocate on a paper folio
@graph.description: What the harness's devils-advocate-watcher means for a paper folio: its claim-bearing kinds and formal tree, the Lean vacuity shapes the Formalist lens looks for, and the paper watchers the adversary sits beside.

@graph.name: proof-simplifier
@graph.title: Proof Simplifier
@graph.description: Analyse small clusters (2–4) of connected proofs to find simplifications: shared lemmas, redundant constructions, factored abstractions, or shorter proof paths through the dependency graph.

@graph.name: math-render-check
@graph.title: Math render check
@graph.description: The math half of the harness's markdown-render-check: grep checks for display math, KaTeX and LaTeX patterns that GitHub's renderer breaks, and the fix recipe for multi-line display equations.

@graph.name: q-usage-watcher
@graph.title: /q-usage-watcher
@graph.description: q-usage integration watcher — detects how each content block treats the substrate parameter $q$ (symbolic / generic-R / real-positive / q > 1 / |q| > 1 / unit-circle / root-of-unity / fixed q_0 / n/a) and cross-checks the detected regime vector against the chapter's narrative-expected profile. Emits per-block `<block>.qa.json` sidecars under the `q-usage-*` criteria and a global witness JSON. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake) from `integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: proof-narrative-lean-equivalence
@graph.title: Proof Narrative ↔ Lean Equivalence Audit
@graph.description: For each content block with both a narrative proof (.md) and a Lean sibling (.lean), verify the two prove the same thing. Detect stub-weakening (Lean claims less than the paper), overreach (Lean claims more than the paper), hypothesis mismatches, and notation drift. Produces a structured equivalence report; no edits.

@graph.name: simulator-math-audit
@graph.title: Simulator Math Audit
@graph.description: Audit simulator content objects against the formal mathematics they visualise — formulas and physical constants must be derived from the paper's canonical sources, never hardcoded in the visualisation.

@graph.name: definition-clarity-audit
@graph.title: definition-clarity-audit
@graph.description: Definition / statement clarity + concision audit. A content block can validate (schema-clean, refs resolve, formal-proof sibling present) and still read badly: the defined term is never emphasised, the definition is buried under paragraphs of motivation, or one `definition` block silently bundles three or four distinct definienda. Use when asked to "bold defined terms", "tighten definitions", "no rambling definitions", "one definition per block", "tight theorem/proposition/lemma statements", or to set up / run a clarity audit. Also runs the inverse audit — a non-`definition` block that secretly carries a definition (`clarity-defn-misplaced`) — plus a statement-purity check (`clarity-stmt-pure`: a theorem/prop/lemma/conjecture carries only its claim; embedded remark / interpretation moves to a follow-on `remark`) and a register check (`clarity-grad-style`: graduate-level formal-math prose — no contractions, second-person, hype, colloquialism, or emoji). Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `clarity-*` criteria via `content/pipeline/definition-clarity-audit.ts`.

@graph.name: category-theory
@graph.title: Category Theory Formalization
@graph.description: Category Theory formalization skill — handles diagram chasing, universal properties, functorial translation, and whiskering in Lean 4.  Integrates with Mathlib's typeclass-centric category theory and provides tactic strategies for commutativity proofs.

@graph.name: chapter-analysis
@graph.title: Chapter Analysis & Formalization
@graph.description: Thorough analysis and Lean 4 formalization of a single manuscript chapter. Extracts all narrative definitions/propositions (excluding remarks), identifies missing glossary terms, writes comprehensive Lean stubs using mathlib, and proves limiting-case and structural theorems where possible.

@graph.name: lean-completeness-audit
@graph.title: Lean Completeness Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit Lean formalization completeness across all papers: verify Lake project setup, check import coverage, identify missing .lean files for content blocks that require them, report formalization gaps, and detect stale witnesses.

@graph.name: lean-proof-review
@graph.title: Lean Proof Review
@graph.description: Review Lean 4 proofs for correctness, style, and completeness. Tracks review scores from multiple reviewers (human and agentic) in proof-objects.json.  Integrates with the agent-review pipeline.

@graph.name: rendering-fixes
@graph.title: Rendering Fixes
@graph.description: Quick-fix reference for common rendering errors found by the rendering-auditor. Agents should consult this when editing content blocks to avoid introducing issues and to fix flagged problems efficiently.

@graph.name: lean-environment-setup
@graph.title: Lean Environment Setup
@graph.description: Sets up and troubleshoots the Lean 4 environment for Claude Code sessions. Ensures elan, lake, lean are installed so the paper-assistant MCP's Lean tools are operational. Handles sandboxed/cloud environments where downloads may be restricted.

@graph.name: paper-importer
@graph.title: Paper Importer
@graph.description: Import external papers from PDF, LaTeX, or arXiv into the content object system. Scans for theorems, definitions, propositions, lemmas, and other formal environments. Generates .ts manifests and .md content files, optionally creates .lean stubs with sorry-bridged proofs citing the original source. Integrates with proof-writer skills so imported theorems can inform and accelerate formalization of the main paper.

@graph.name: proposition-consolidation-audit
@graph.title: /proposition-consolidation-audit
@graph.description: Scan a chapter (or the whole paper) for propositions/theorems/lemmas that overlap structurally — same boxed equation under different parametrisations, near-identical proof skeletons, explicit "specialisation of"/"case of"/"corollary of" wording in `.md`, or high-overlap on (uses, cites, tags). Reports candidates for consolidation: parent → corollary, true duplicates, mergeable statements. Run after large-scale chapter work or when the user notices the exposition has accreted special cases.

@graph.name: compute-author
@graph.title: Compute-author skill — read before writing compute code
@graph.description: Pre-work briefing + durable patterns for anyone writing or modifying compute scripts (or the native crates they call). Read this BEFORE you write or change compute code — it covers precision discipline, the native↔script boundary cost, exact-arithmetic choices (big-integer vs big-rational vs arbitrary-precision float), algebraic-preflight requirements before optimization shortcuts, and witness-emission discipline. Sibling to `compute-audit` (post-hoc); this skill is pre-work.

@graph.name: lean-substantive-pass
@graph.title: /lean-substantive-pass
@graph.description: Convert abstract `holds : Prop` / `claim : Prop` placeholder Lean stubs into typed sub-claim contexts with manuscript-semantic field names. Three escalation levels: hand-craft per-block (highest fidelity), bulk-script split on numbered sub-claims, and docstring enrichment (extract first-sentence summaries from .md). Use this skill after `lean-generation` has created the placeholder stubs and the backlog is structurally closed.

@graph.name: hypothesis-generation
@graph.title: Scientific Hypothesis Generation
@graph.description: Formulate evidence-bounded scientific questions, candidate hypotheses, rival explanations, causal or associational claims, discriminating predictions, measurements, and preregistration-ready analysis plans. Use when turning observations or preliminary findings into transparent, testable research plans without treating hypotheses as facts.

@graph.name: scientific-critical-thinking
@graph.title: Scientific Critical Thinking
@graph.description: Evaluate scientific claims and evidence quality. Use for assessing experimental design validity, identifying biases and confounders, applying evidence grading frameworks (GRADE, Cochrane Risk of Bias), or teaching critical analysis. Best for understanding evidence quality, identifying flaws. For formal peer review writing use peer-review.

@graph.name: scientific-visualization
@graph.title: Scientific Visualization
@graph.description: Create and audit truthful, accessible, publication-ready scientific figures with Matplotlib, Seaborn, or Plotly. Use for figure design, multi-panel layouts, uncertainty and missing-data displays, color/contrast review, image metadata validation, and journal export planning.

@graph.name: reference-dataset-ingestion
@graph.title: Reference dataset ingestion
@graph.description: Ingest a published REFERENCE dataset — a constants table such as CODATA, AME or PDG — into a library entry whose values are addressable in prose as {{ <instance>.library.<entry>.<slug> }}, with edition, source, sha256 and licence recorded. Use when a paper quotes a physical constant, when a value is hard-coded in a script or registry, or before adding a "vendored snapshot" of someone else's numbers.

@graph.name: lean-formal-edges
@graph.title: Lean formal edges (elaborated)
@graph.description: Extract ELABORATED formal dependencies between a folio's lean.ref declarations — the trustworthy replacement for the lexical `--scan` cache. Use when the formal graph matters (impact analysis, staleness, a blueprint's \uses), when `lean-formal-graph` reports source "scan", or before trusting a type/value split.

@graph.name: lean-html-docs
@graph.title: Lean HTML docs — the `lean` directory's visualiser
@graph.description: Build and publish the visualiser of a folio's declared `lean` directory: the package's doc-gen4 HTML render, staged under the folio's site and wrapped in the harness navbar and rail. Use when a folio's Lean docs are missing, stale, or published without the harness chrome, or when declaring a `lean` directory and its `coverage.visualiser`.

@graph.name: Publish a folio's Lean render with the harness chrome
@graph.summary: Build the visualiser of a folio's declared `lean` directory — the Lake package's doc-gen4 HTML render — and put it inside the folio's built site with the harness navbar and rail.
@graph.description:
Build the visualiser of a folio's declared `lean` directory — the Lake package's doc-gen4 HTML render — and put it inside the folio's built site with the harness navbar and rail.

Two steps in two lanes. The build is a Lake run over the folio's warm olean cache: expensive, and able to damage the cache (a Lake build over an untraced restore evicts it), so it sits with the Lean toolchain and refuses rather than risks. The publish is a file pass over the build's output that cannot touch the cache; it sits with the build pipeline, after the site is built and before the chrome check and deploy, where `stage-folio-local.ts` rails the folio's own pages.

Only End_Ready publishes: a refused guard, a failed build and an unrailed page are each reported as such, never as a complete site without Lean docs.

Build the doc-gen4 render over the warm cache
No render — refused or failed; nothing published
Stage the render under the site and rail every page
Lean pages ready for the chrome check and deploy

@graph.name: typologies
@graph.summary: The graph typologies a harness declares it owns, one node per kind, so no central registry names another harness's subgraph types. Loaded across the instances on first use.

@graph.name: validators
@graph.summary: The validators a harness's code provides, one node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks and the Zod export that checks it, joined onto the kinds on first use.

@graph.name: qa-checkers
@graph.summary: The QA checkers a harness provides, one node per criterion naming the table that holds the code; registered for a folio through its dependency tree.

@graph.name: pipeline-plugins
@graph.summary: The generic pipeline slots a harness fills, one node per slot naming the table of implementations; registered for a folio through its dependency tree.

@graph.name: block-kinds
@graph.summary: The block kinds a harness's adapter owns, one node per kind carrying its label prefix, RDF types, profile and builder. Discovered across the instances; no module lists them.

@graph.name: content-adapters
@graph.summary: The block vocabularies a harness owns, one node per vocabulary carrying its companion roles and whether the platform's code types it. Discovered across the instances; no module lists them.

@graph.name: tools
@graph.summary: Tool definitions — themselves nodes in the KG, per the repo taxonomy.

@graph.name: skills
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Skills: the instructions an Actor follows to carry out a Task.

@graph.name: processes
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Processes: BPMN diagrams that coordinate Tasks, and the decision tables their gateways compute from.

@graph.name: scenarios
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Roles: the responsibilities an Actor takes on, and who takes them on.

@graph.name: methodology
@graph.summary: Judgement methodologies, adopted whole and kept independent — parallel ways to reach a decision, selected by context.

@graph.name: docs
@graph.summary: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph — how the harness works, what its directories hold, how a process runs. Rendered by the plain just-the-docs pipeline. Distinct from `folio`, which is content an author CREATES using the graph; the difference is the SUBJECT, not the format. An L1 library's catalogue is `library/`; a note about it is a `folio`; the page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`.

@graph.name: schemas
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Node Schemas: files that state the shape other files must have.

@graph.name: qa
@graph.summary: QA verdicts and their projections — kg-qa audits, block and translation QA, qa-witness documents for the docs site, the viewer-navbar audit, result roll-ups and test runs; every `$schema` family is named in `nodeSchemas`, which is the list — a count here would be a second one, and it was already wrong by one before `viewer-nav-qa/v1` was added. Generated; never hand-edited.

@graph.name: attestations
@graph.summary: QA attestations — the judgements a QA family carries across runs (pair attestations, voice reviews, agent and human verdicts, bibliography verifications and human reviews), one `qa-attestations/v1` file per subject, mirroring the derived family's tree. Kept on main where deleting derived results cannot reach them; each entry pins the hash it attested, so a stale one is detectable.

@graph.name: code
@graph.summary: Source code -- the modules, scripts and entry points an instance holds. Declared so that code is scannable at all: an undeclared file is one no checker has a reason to look at. Being declared here says nothing about whether a Tool node claims it, which is a separate question and a separate axis.

@graph.name: library
@graph.summary: L1 source content — one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`. Every knowledge-graph reference to a source resolves through here, never to a loose path or a bare URL.

@graph.name: software-library
@graph.summary: Outside libraries a layer imports or vendors -- one generated `software-library` node per library per layer, with the version and sha512 its `bun.lock` pins, its SPDX licence, its range, whether it is a dev dependency, the files that import it and the shim that types it. Shares its core with `tool-release`.

@graph.name: voices
@graph.summary: Editorial voice profiles — one JSON each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-voice/v1"`. Every rule cites the ingested source or KG node it was derived from. Opt-in per folio.

@graph.name: translation-sources
@graph.summary: POT templates, PO catalogues and their `TranslationNode` manifests, one directory per target locale. The INPUT to injection; the rendered output is ordinary content that declares its own `lang`.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.summary: SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1): local terms with definitions and codes, linked to external SKOS schemes by exactMatch rather than copied. Rendered on the glossary/ page.

@graph.name: references
@graph.summary: Bibliographic references, one folio-reference/v1 node per work: a CSL-JSON item at `references/<key>`, the IRI every `\cite{key}` already points at, read as Dublin Core and BIBO through its JSON-LD.

@graph.name: editor-checkers
@graph.summary: The checks and editor settings a harness provides to the ✍ suggest editor, one node per content profile, each naming the code (`path.ts#Export`) the editor loads for that profile's blocks.

@graph.name: lean
@graph.summary: A folio's Lean 4 formalisation: Lake packages, their modules and the declarations in them. Declared by the folio that holds the packages; this harness owns the kind, the Lean tools and the rendering (doc-gen4 HTML wrapped in the harness rail).

@graph.title: Lean authoring agent
@graph.description: Writes and repairs the Lean 4 formalization — translating narrative mathematics into declarations, keeping the build green, and curating what is staged for upstream.

@graph.title: Compute authoring agent
@graph.description: Writes and audits the computation scripts and simulators that produce witnessed values, and keeps the paper's numbers and its computations from drifting apart.

@graph.title: Proof review agent
@graph.description: Reviews proofs — narrative and formal — for gaps, vacuity, redundancy and divergence between the two renderings of the same claim.

@graph.title: Lean toolchain
@graph.description: Elaborates and checks the formal half of a paper folio. Answers only what Lean can answer.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-docs
@graph.description: This instance's own reader-facing pages: the guide to writing a paper, which documents this instance's own process (`processes/content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn`). Composed THROUGH just-the-docs (`composed: true`, as the content core's own docs directory is), so its pages land in the platform's site under this instance's name with the sidebar, search and layout. `docs.json` here declares the `docs-source` the platform's one docs-page run reads: each `source/<group>-<slug>/` renders into `<group>/<slug>.md` beside it, and `compose-docs` leaves `source/` itself out.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-qa-checkers
@graph.description: The QA checkers this instance's Lean tooling provides, one folio-qa-checker/v1 node per criterion, naming COST_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-cost.ts, and the maths checkers: VACUITY_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (Lean vacuity, four criteria), RENDER_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (render-math-mode-envelope), TRIVIALITY_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (proof-not-machine-trivial), EXTENDED_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (the paper proof-*, canonical-* and compute-* criteria), USES_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS (uses-formal-coverage, lean-ref-owns-decl), Q_USAGE_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-q-usage.ts (the seven q-usage-* criteria, run on their own by pipeline/q-usage-audit.ts) and WALL_AUTOMATED_CHECKERS in pipeline/qa-checkers-wall.ts (framework-canonical and the §7c archimedean wall: wall-side-correct, wall-base-ring-minimal). Registered for a folio by loadContributions through its dependency tree.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-editor-checkers
@graph.description: The ✍ suggest editor's checks and Crepe settings for this instance's content profiles, one folio-editor-checker/v1 node per profile naming the code (`path.ts#Export`) the editor loads. Today it holds one node: `paper-latex`, the LaTeX syntax checker and the Crepe repairs for paper math. The kind is declared in typologies/editor-checkers.json and its validator in validators/editor-checker.json.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-validators
@graph.description: The validators this instance's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each, naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks and the Zod export that checks it: `conjecture-register` for `folio-conjecture-register/v1` and `editor-checker` for `folio-editor-checker/v1`.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-pipeline-plugins
@graph.description: The generic pipeline slots this instance fills, one folio-pipeline-plugin/v1 node per slot, naming PIPELINE_IMPLEMENTATIONS in pipeline/plugin-slots.ts. Registered for a folio by loadContributions through its dependency tree.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-translations
@graph.description: The gettext side of folio-assistant-sci's own strings, one directory per target locale. `block-kinds.pot`/`.po`, the headings of the block kinds this instance declares in block-kinds/, keyed `msgctxt "block-kind:<kind>"` with the node's English `heading` as msgid, and `processes/<process>.pot`, the text of this layer's BPMN processes. Locale headings live in the translation graph, and kinds are not centrally managed, so the catalogue sits with the kinds rather than in cat-harness/translations/.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-block-typologies
@graph.description: The paper adapter's math block kinds — the ones whose assertion is a formal mathematical claim (definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture, proof), one folio-block-kind/v1 node per file. Kinds are discoverable and not centrally managed: cat-harness/schemas/block-kinds.ts finds these by scanning every instance's declared block-kinds graph.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-content-adapters
@graph.description: The `mathpaper` block VOCABULARY's node, folio-content-adapter/v1: its name, its companion roles (md, ts, lean) and that cat-harness's code types it. The seven formal-claim kinds in block-kinds/ name it; core's document kinds name core's own `document` adapter. cat-harness/schemas/block-kinds.ts derives CONTENT_ADAPTERS from the typed nodes, and block-qa.ts derives ADAPTER_COMPANION_ROLES. The vocabulary is a node; the server adapter class stays in contentAdapters.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-typologies
@graph.description: The graph typologies folio-assistant-sci owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file. There is no central registry for subgraph types: a harness declares its own in a kinds/ graph.

@graph.name: library
@graph.description: Ingested L1 source material for the sciences: `milnorlink`, the source text the `milnor-exposition-standard` skill reads; the Lean-autoformalization papers this layer's methodology nodes cite as `evidence`; papers on extracting mathematics from PDFs; and the CODATA 2022 constants table. `image-verdicts.json` holds the image-role judgements for this library's documents. The id is `library`, the conventional one, so this entry overrides the default rather than joining it: overrides match on id, never on path, so a distinct id at the same path would yield two entries for one directory and every fan-out consumer would scan it twice.

@graph.name: sci-extracted-references
@graph.description: The reference lists of the papers in `library/`, split into one folio-reference/v1 node per entry with `provenance: extracted`. Each node is `<doc-id>.r<n>.json`, `<n>` being the printed number of a numbered list (so `[12]` in a paper's text is `.r12`) or the position in an author-year one; `derivedFrom` names the section file the entry was read from. GENERATED by scripts/extract-references.ts from the library text, never hand-edited: `check:extracted-references` fails on any difference. The text is PDF extraction, so the raw entry is always kept whole in `note`, and `title`, `author`, `issued`, `DOI` and `URL` are set only where the entry's shape makes them unambiguous; a field the extractor could not read with confidence is absent, not guessed. Listed and exported, with every other `references` directory, by folio-assistant-core's bibliography viewer.

@graph.name: sci-methodologies
@graph.description: The methodologies this layer adopts from its own library: external, named methods for formalising mathematics in Lean. A method belongs to the layer whose job it describes (`methodology-adoption` §4), so these sit apart from cat-harness's and core's methodologies. Each node renders the METHOD and states where the rendering stops; the paper's tools and numbers are not adopted.

@graph.name: skills
@graph.description: The skills this layer owns: the paper content adapter's skills (`content/folio-paper-adapter/`, with `authoring-math`, `hypothesis-generation`, `scientific-critical-thinking` and `scientific-visualization` beside it), plus `lean/`, `data/` and the `voices/` subgraph, which `skills/skills.json` declares from within. Declared here explicitly on 2026-10-04 (bean `g2sv`, issue #2106). The directory was already reachable through the `skills` entry of `DEFAULT_DIRECTORIES`, which `ownDirectories` seeds for every instance and marks `declaredBy: (default)`, so `skill_list` already served its packages. A read-only analysis of the qou folio nonetheless reported it as undeclared and reachable only through `known-skills.ts`, because the declaration file was the only place the analysis looked, and that file said nothing. A convention is not visible from the declaration a reader opens, and a reader should not have to know the fallback to learn that this instance's largest graph exists. The id is `skills`, the CONVENTIONAL one, so this entry OVERRIDES the default rather than joining it. The reason is the one the `library` entry above gives: overrides match on id and never on path, so a distinct id at the same path would make two entries for one directory.

@graph.name: sci-adapters
@graph.description: The PAPER content adapter: `PaperContentAdapter` and its Lean tool registrar, with its LaTeX, Lean and suggest code and its in-process tools. `dependents: skip` because a dependent gets its adapter by DECLARING a `contentType`, resolved through `BUILTIN_ADAPTERS` by variable path, rather than by inheriting this directory to scan.

@graph.name: sci-scripts
@graph.description: This instance's scripts: its checkout checks (`check-lean-dirs.ts`, `check-editor-checkers.ts`, `check-workflows-security.ts`, `extract-references.ts`), Lean helpers (`setup-lean-toolchain.sh`, `lean-audit.ts`, `lean-coverage.ts`, `lsi-lean-decls.ts`), the Lean cache service (`lake-cache.sh` — the `lean-cache` tool — `reseed-lean-cache.sh`, `lake-cache-fetch.sh`, `lake-cache-produce.py`, `lake-cache-fetch-multi.py` and their `.bat` entry points, which only a Lean folio runs; they read and write the branch family `cat/folio-assistant-sci/lake-cache/<pkg>`), and `tests/`, which hold the harness's code, imported down from cat-harness, against this instance's paper processes, decision tables, pipeline plugins and contributed checkers.

@graph.name: folio-assistant-sci-libraries
@graph.title: Software libraries
@graph.description: The outside libraries this layer's code imports: one `software-library/1.0.0` node per dependency in `package.json`, with the version and sha512 that `bun.lock` pins, the registry tarball, the SPDX licence read from the installed package, the range, whether it is a dev dependency, the files that import it (`usedBy`) and the `types/*.d.ts` shim that types it. GENERATED, never hand-edited: `bun run cat libraries:derive` writes it and `libraries:check` fails on a stale node, an import no node names, and a shim no node names. The kind is cat-harness's (one outside-software core shared with `tool-release`), and the writer and the gate are cat-harness-tools' (`scripts/libraries.ts`); this layer keeps its own nodes because it pins its own versions.

@graph.name: sci-lean
@graph.description: The Lean templates this harness's tooling fills: today `formal-edges.lean.tmpl`, which pipeline/formal-edges.ts writes into a folio's own `.lake/` and elaborates there. Declared with graph typology `lean`, the kind this instance owns for Lean sources (typologies/lean.json). The Tools (`lean-html-docs`, `lean-render-publish`), the process (`lean-docs-publish`) and the skill (`lean-html-docs`) are what a FOLIO's `lean` directory gets: its doc-gen4 render, published under the folio's site in the harness rail. `.tmpl`, never `.lean`: the platform tracks no Lean content, and lean-decl-starts-are-shared.test.ts holds it to that.

@graph.name: folio-templates
@graph.description: The PAPER profile of the files `folio_init` writes into a new folio: `paper/` holds the Lean build, lake-cache restore and blueprint workflows and the `.github/scripts` they call, written into a paper folio after the `document/` profile the tools layer keeps. Only a paper folio is given them, and the paper profile is this layer's. The id is the tools layer's `folio-templates`, so this directory is a member of that subgraph and `init-folio` finds it by id across the checkout, never by a path naming this layer. `{{assistant}}`, `{{folio}}`, `{{platform_git}}` and `{{platform_repo}}` are substituted at write time. Declared `code`: executable sources whose target is another repository. `dependents: skip` -- a folio inherits them through `folio_init`, not by owning a copy.

@graph.name: sci-tools
@graph.description: The science layer's Tool nodes. One `<id>/<id>.ts` (or `.json`) per folder: LaTeX build and checks, the Lean build, cache, audit and publish tools, and the proof-object tools. Reached by the harness through tool auto-discovery (cat-harness/tools/discover.ts), never by an import.

@graph.name: sci-sources
@graph.description: Source descriptors (`folio-source-descriptor/v1`): how to ENUMERATE Lean mathlib and ask it for a SUBSET. A descriptor is ABOUT one corpus and the instance that holds or catalogues that corpus owns it — the schema stays in cat-harness. Its far-apart sibling, WHO IRIS, is in who-iris: a mathlib declaration needs its import closure (`subsetIsSelfContained: false`), one identifier system, a local module graph.

@graph.name: sci-processes
@graph.description: The BPMN and DMN this layer OWNS: the paper's content processes, grouped by concern exactly as the harness groups its own (`processes/<group>/`, a DMN in `processes/<group>/decisions/`). `content/authoring-a-paper.bpmn` with `content/decisions/lean-build-gate.dmn`, `content/atomic-mass-drift-check.bpmn` and `content/lean-docs-publish.bpmn`. They name Lean and paper skills that live here, which cat-harness cannot reach. Their calls and skill refs that stay generic point DOWN through core to the harness.

@graph.name: scenarios
@graph.description: Scenarios: the roles an actor takes on, in `roles.json`, the user stories told as them, in `stories.json`, and the actors in `actors/`. The compute-authoring-agent, lean-authoring-agent and proof-review-agent roles live here, and this layer's `address-*` voices point at them.

@graph.name: qa
@graph.description: What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another.

@graph.name: attestations
@graph.description: The judgement half of this instance's QA verdicts, kept on main: the `pair_attestations` that were carried inside its `kg-qa/v1` sidecars, one `qa-attestations/v1` file per subject at `kg-qa/<mirrored subject path>.attestations.json`. Schema: cat-harness `schemas/qa-attestations.ts`. dependents: reproduce, for the reason the `qa` entry gives.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.description: Science's generated glossary (`glossary/generated/folio-assistant-sci/`): candidate `folio-glossary/v1` schemes extracted from this layer's tools, skills, BPMN activities and DMN decisions by core's `glossary:page`. A scheme is keyed by (instance, scheme), and each layer holds its own glossary.

@graph.name: agent-instructions
@graph.title: AGENTS.md — folio-assistant-sci
@graph.description: Cold start for work in this layer. Source material a folio READS, never mathematics this repository authors — and the placement rule: a repository named for one catalogue is not a place to keep things belonging to another.

@graph.name: readme
@graph.title: folio-assistant-sci
@graph.description: What this layer holds and how it is reached.

@graph.name: checkout-scripts
@graph.title: package.json — folio-assistant-sci
@graph.description: The checkout scripts this instance's code runs, under `checkoutScripts`. Each command is relative to the downstream checkout root; a downstream that mounts this instance reads them with `bun run cat`.

@graph.name: check-dependencies
@graph.title: Dependency probe
@graph.description: Report which of the harness's optional and required dependencies are present on this machine, and what each unmet one blocks.

inputs.name: required_only
inputs.description: Report only the dependencies without which the harness cannot run.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Per-dependency: present, absent, or could not be determined.

@graph.name: content-manifest-validate
@graph.title: Content manifest validation
@graph.description: Validate the block manifests under a path against their schemas.

inputs.name: targetPath
inputs.description: A paper or chapter directory; absent, every paper the folio declares.

inputs.name: strict
inputs.description: Treat warnings as errors.

outputs.name: issues
outputs.description: One line per issue, with its block and file. Exit 2 means NO FOLIO WAS FOUND — could-not-determine, never valid.

@graph.name: headless-render-qc
@graph.title: Headless render QC (Playwright)
@graph.description: Drive a folio's built viewer in headless Chromium and report the blocks whose diagrams, SVGs, LaTeX math or markdown do not render — with `--screenshot` to save the pictures.

@graph.name: latex-image
@graph.title: Compile LaTeX in a container
@graph.description: Compile a rendered paper's `main.tex` with latexmk inside a TeX Live (full) image, for a host with Docker but no TeX engine. The image carries TeX Live, latexmk, Pandoc, latexdiff, graphviz and poppler-utils; it does not run the content pipeline, which renders the chapters on the host first.

inputs.description: The rendered paper's top-level `.tex`, relative to the checkout.

outputs.name: pdf

@graph.name: latex-overfull
@graph.title: LaTeX overfull-box report
@graph.description: Turn a pdflatex log's Overfull \hbox warnings into a located, actionable report, with a threshold so a long tail of trivial overruns does not bury the real ones.

inputs.name: log
inputs.description: The pdflatex log to read.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Ignore overruns below this size

inputs.name: max
inputs.description: Fail above this count, for use as a gate.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Located overfull boxes. Requires a build log: with no log there is nothing to read, which is could-not-determine rather than clean.

@graph.name: latex-preflight
@graph.title: LaTeX preflight
@graph.description: Lint TeX source for the pdflatex-compile failure classes a permissive AST parser accepts — the ones that pass validation and then break the build.

inputs.name: warn
inputs.description: Report without failing — for a corpus not yet clean.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Compile-breaking hazards, located. A clean run here is not a successful compile; it is the absence of these classes.

@graph.name: latexmk-compile
@graph.title: LaTeX compilation (latexmk)
@graph.description: Compile LaTeX source documents into PDF using latexmk with safe shell-escape isolation across CI events.

inputs.description: The TeX source file to compile (e.g. main.tex).

inputs.name: args
inputs.description: Additional arguments to forward to latexmk.

outputs.name: pdf

@graph.name: lean-audit
@graph.title: Lean vacuity audit
@graph.description: Inspect Lean declarations chapter by chapter for proofs that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and still carry no mathematical content — assuming what they claim, concluding something trivially true, or resting on a false premise.

inputs.name: chapter
inputs.description: One chapter instead of the whole corpus.

inputs.name: checkAxioms
inputs.description: Axiom-cleanliness is a separate question from vacuity: a proof can be axiom-clean and still assume its conclusion.

outputs.name: findings
outputs.description: Sorry inventory and trivial-truth detections. Sibling of `lean-coverage`, not an alternative to it: that one COUNTS what is proved, this one asks whether a proof says anything.

@graph.name: lean-build
@graph.title: Lean build
@graph.description: Build every Lean project in the workspace from the root Lake manifest, so cross-package dependencies resolve against it rather than a possibly-stale per-paper manifest. Writes a committable build-status sidecar every run.

inputs.name: paper
inputs.description: Build one paper instead of all of them.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Fetch the Mathlib cache first. A from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes against ~2 for a restore.

inputs.name: update
inputs.description: Run `lake update` before building.

inputs.name: logDir
inputs.description: Where logs and the status sidecar go.

outputs.name: status
outputs.description: `lean-build-status.json` — committable, so a green build is distinguishable from one nobody ran.

@graph.name: lean-cache
@graph.title: Lake olean cache
@graph.description: Restore, verify, seed and diagnose the prebuilt `.lake/` artefacts for a Lean package. Always try `restore` first: a from-source Mathlib build is 30–60 minutes, a restore about two.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: The verb. `doctor` tells a restore that silently missed from one that worked.

inputs.name: lakeRoot
inputs.description: The package whose `.lake/` is acted on.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: A real hit, a miss, or a diagnosis — never a miss that reads as a hit.

@graph.name: lean-coverage
@graph.title: Lean coverage
@graph.description: Count how many provable blocks — theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary — carry a full Lean proof rather than a sorry, per paper. The completeness half of the Lean audit: what is formalised, and what is still a gap.

inputs.name: paper
inputs.description: One paper instead of all.

inputs.name: contentRoot
inputs.description: Where content blocks live. not a Lean project root.

outputs.name: coverage
outputs.description: Provable blocks, and how many are sorry-free. A count, not a verdict: a sorry-free proof can still be vacuous, which is the sibling node's question.

@graph.name: lean-formal-edges
@graph.title: Formal edges from the Lean build
@graph.description: Extract ELABORATED formal dependencies between a folio's lean.ref declarations (LeanArchitect's rule over the folio's own lean.ref set). Needs a Lean toolchain and a built Lake project. Tagged declarations missing from the build are reported, never recorded as dependency-free; with ingest the result is recorded in the formal cache as source "elaborated".

inputs.name: lake_dir
inputs.description: The folio's Lake project directory (holds lakefile.* and .lake/).

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Content root to collect lean.ref targets from (default: the folio's declared one).

inputs.name: ingest
inputs.description: Record the result in the formal cache as source "elaborated".

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: The extracted edges, or why they could not be determined — never an empty edge set in place of a failure.

@graph.name: lean-html-docs
@graph.title: Build a Lean package's HTML docs (doc-gen4)
@graph.description: Build the doc-gen4 HTML render of a folio's Lake package — the visualiser of a declared `lean` directory — with `lake -R -Kenv=dev build <Lib>:docs`, cache-aware: refuses while another lake/lean process holds `.lake/`, refuses on a restored tree that carries no traces (a Lake build there EVICTS the cache), checks or restores the warm cache first, and enables a sentinel-commented doc-gen4 `[[require]]` for this build only, restoring the lakefile on exit. Never runs `lake update`. Output: `<lake-root>/.lake/build/doc`.

inputs.name: lakeRoot
inputs.description: The Lake package directory whose lakefile requires (or sentinel-comments) doc-gen4, e.g. `folio/quantum-observable-universe/lean`.

inputs.name: lib
inputs.description: The `lean_lib` to document, e.g. `QOU` (a Lean library name: alphanumerics, dot, underscore, hyphen). Repeat for several.

inputs.name: platform
inputs.description: The index checkout holding `lake-cache.sh`. Default `$FOLIO_ASSISTANT_ROOT`.

inputs.name: restore
inputs.description: Restore the warm cache first (about 2 minutes) instead of only checking it.

inputs.name: allowCold
inputs.description: Build without a warm cache: Mathlib from source, 30-60 minutes before doc-gen4 starts.

inputs.name: dryRun
inputs.description: Run every guard, print the build command, build nothing.

outputs.name: render
outputs.description: `<lake-root>/.lake/build/doc`, doc-gen4's output, printed as the last line. Feed it to `lean-render-publish`.

@graph.name: lean-kg-publish
@graph.title: Publish the dynamic Lean viewer: doc-gen4 declaration data as knowledge-graph shards
@graph.description: Ingest doc-gen4's per-module declaration data (`.lake/build/doc-data/declaration-data-<Module>.bmp`) into JSON-LD shards — one per module, with declaration nodes, `imports` edges and `formalizes` edges to the content blocks whose `lean.ref` names each declaration — and publish them under the folio's site with a single viewer page that loads modules, signature chunks and the search list on demand. Signatures are chunked 500 declarations per file so a 12,804-declaration module stays usable. With `--base` it writes a STAGING overlay: only modules whose content hash differs from the published base, plus `overlay.json`; the viewer loads the rest from the base. Rails the viewer page with the same pass as `lean-render-publish`.

inputs.description: doc-gen4's `.lake/build/doc-data` from `lean-html-docs`.

inputs.name: site
inputs.description: The folio's built site.

inputs.name: route
inputs.description: Where under the site. Default `lean`.

inputs.name: module
inputs.description: A module root to keep (`qou` keeps `QOU`). Repeat for several.

inputs.name: contentRoot
inputs.description: Content tree whose blocks' `lean.ref` become `formalizes` edges.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: `owner/repo` for block links.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.description: Branch or sha for block links.

inputs.name: contentPrefix
inputs.description: Path of the content root inside the repo, for block links.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: Published `data/` of the base graph; enables the STAGING overlay.

inputs.name: externalBase
inputs.description: Where links into pruned modules go. Default the community mathlib4 docs.

inputs.name: homeLabel
inputs.description: The rail's home row.

inputs.name: instance

@graph.name: lean-render-publish
@graph.title: Publish a Lean render under a folio site, with the harness rail
@graph.description: Stage a doc-gen4 render under a folio's built site (`<site>/<route>/`, default `lean/`) and give every page the harness navbar and rail by running `cat-harness/scripts/rail-standalone-pages.ts --foreign-site` over the site — the same rail `stage-folio-local.ts` applies to the folio's own pages. Leaves out Lake's `.hash`/`.trace` bookkeeping, marks doc-gen4's iframe navbar and `find/` redirect `folio-navbar: none` so no rail is drawn inside the sidebar, adds a layout shim so the rail does not cover doc-gen4's fixed sidebar, and with `--modules` prunes to the folio's own modules, repointing links into dropped ones to the community docs. Then asserts every staged page is railed or declined.

inputs.name: docs
inputs.description: The doc-gen4 render, `lean-html-docs`'s output.

inputs.name: site

inputs.name: route
inputs.description: Where under the site. Default `lean`.

inputs.name: module
inputs.description: A Lake package whose module root to keep (`qou` keeps `QOU/`, matched case-insensitively). Repeat for several. Default: keep everything.

inputs.name: externalBase
inputs.description: Where links into pruned modules go. Default the community mathlib4 docs.

inputs.name: homeLabel
inputs.description: The rail's home row: the folio's instance name, e.g. `qou`.

inputs.name: instance
inputs.description: Rail as this instance's own site (its name, mark and graphs), as rail-standalone-pages.ts --instance.

inputs.name: platform
inputs.description: The index checkout holding the rail pass. Default `$FOLIO_ASSISTANT_ROOT`, then the nearest ancestor that has it.

inputs.name: noRail
inputs.description: Stage only; the caller rails the site itself.

outputs.name: pages
outputs.description: `<site>/<route>/`, railed, plus the rail's shared data under `<site>/assets/navbar/`.

A preview, never a publish build. Run from the folio.

inputs.name: base
inputs.description: The ref to diff against. Default `origin/main`.

inputs.name: chapters

inputs.name: preload

outputs.name: preview
outputs.description: `<out>/changed.pdf`, `<out>/<chapter>.diff-color.pdf` and `.diff-plain.pdf`, with the logs and `<out>/build.log` beside them. The render also rewrites the folio's `chapters/` and `main.tex`.

@graph.name: tex-install
@graph.title: Install TeX Live in a sandbox
@graph.description: Install TeX Live (full) and latexmk where no TeX engine is present, disabling the firewalled launchpad PPAs that otherwise abort `apt-get update`. Idempotent: does nothing when pdflatex and memoize.sty are already present. Run it in the background. pdflatex unpacks early but is not usable until the post-install format build ends (`kpsewhich memoize.sty` returning a path is the ready signal).

outputs.name: engine
outputs.description: A `pdflatex --version` line on success. The installed packages are system-wide.

@graph.name: tex-snippet-validate
@graph.title: TeX snippet validation (AST)
@graph.description: Parse every `tex` snippet in a folio's blocks and report what will not compile — structural, not textual: it reads an AST rather than matching patterns. Complementary to `latex-preflight`, which gates a main.tex before a compile, and to `latex-overfull`, which reads a log after one.

inputs.name: paper
inputs.description: One folio by slug. Absent, every folio the content root holds.

inputs.name: file
inputs.description: A single `.md` block, for the narrow case.

inputs.name: compile
inputs.description: Also compile each snippet with pdflatex — needs a TeX distribution, which the base `requires` does NOT claim.

inputs.name: warningsLog
inputs.description: Write a QA-compatible log to this path.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Per snippet, what will not compile. With no folio to scan it reports `Files scanned: 0` and exits 2 (could-not-determine). Read the scanned count before reading the verdict.

@graph.name: tex-source-audit
@graph.title: TeX-source hazard audit
@graph.description: Catch the source patterns that crash pdflatex but read as ordinary prose — a bare `_` or `^` in a bibliography field, `|` inside a markdown table cell where it is also the column separator, a `$…$` span across two lines, markdown link syntax inside a fenced tex block, a double subscript.

inputs.name: strict
inputs.description: Exit 1 on any finding, for use as a gate.

outputs.name: report
outputs.description: Hazards with file and line, plus a committed sidecar. Run where no folio exists it says `No .md files found … refusing to report success. This audits a FOLIO's content; folio-assistant is the platform.` and exits 2 (could-not-determine).
